title: Stanford bunny (rendered)
author: Marcel Padilla
attribution: Derived from the Stanford Bunny STL by Makerbot (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Stanford_Bunny.stl), CC BY 3.0.

geometry.units: render units (mesh normalized so its longest axis = 2.0), not metric

render.poses: known camera-to-world (NeRF transforms.json), so structure-from-motion is skipped
render.material: matte, high-frequency procedural texture (a scanning target)
render.training: Brush (from main), 30000 iters, 500k cap, alpha-mode transparent

caveats: SYNTHETIC, not a photographic capture: a known mesh rendered from known poses and reconstructed as a splat. Geometry and appearance are exact (not invented), but this is a render, not a real scene.
Licensed CC-BY-3.0 (not 4.0) because it is a derivative of a CC BY 3.0 mesh; credit Makerbot as above.
The colourful texture is a deliberate scanning target (matte, high-frequency), chosen so reconstruction is crisp, not for realism.
